### Tom Ron

Tom is a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Amazon Web Services, in Frontier AI Engineering, specializing in Amazon Quick. He partners with large enterprise customers to deliver AI-powered solutions at scale. Helping organizations automate complex workflows, unlock insights from unstructured data, and accelerate business outcomes with Generative AI. (edited)

entries.title: Asynchronous patterns for calling Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents in serverless pipelines
entries.content:
Asynchronous invocation patterns for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents in serverless pipelines remove idle compute costs while your AI agent processes requests. A common example is document validation: in a real-estate financing back office, an agent can read a property record or loan contract, reason about whether the information is complete and consistent, and return a verdict that downstream steps act on. [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/) provides a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model.

These agents introduce a characteristic that traditional pipeline steps do not have: they think for a while before they answer. How long depends on the prompt, the model, and the document, but it’s rarely instant, and that latency changes how you should call it. The most common first implementation is a compute service, such as an [AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/) function, that invokes the agent and waits for the response. While that function waits, it does nothing, but it is still running, and you are billed for every second of it.

It helps to see where the cost actually lands, because the two sides of the call are billed differently. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, has a consumption-based model that doesn’t charge for CPU while the agent is idle. For instance, while it waits on a large language model to generate a response, or on a tool or Model Context Protocol (MCP) call to return, you are billed for memory during that time, but not for CPU. The compute service that called the agent has no such behavior. A Lambda function, container, or [Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/) (Amazon EC2) instance that issues a synchronous call sits blocked. It holds (and pays for) its full compute allocation until the agent responds. So the waste is not on the agent side. It’s the caller, idling on an open connection.

That makes the caller’s cost track the agent’s runtime. A function that blocks on the agent is billed for essentially the entire processing time, whereas a function that starts the agent and returns is billed only for the brief dispatch. The fix is to release the caller’s compute during the wait and resume the pipeline only when the agent has a result. In this post, we show three patterns that do this (task-token callback, direct service integration, and durable function) and contrast them with the blocking anti-pattern.

## An example pipeline

To compare the patterns on equal footing, we run each one through the same pipeline and change only the step that calls the agent. The pipeline is a deliberately simple, made-up scenario (validating documents for real-estate financing) chosen to keep the orchestration clear. It’s not the point of the post. It stands in for any workflow that calls an agent (or another slow service) and then acts on the result, so picture your own use case in its place.

The pipeline has five stages:

1. **Extract**: An AWS Lambda function performs optical character recognition (OCR) and text extraction on the document. (Extraction is simulated, so the scenario runs without real documents.)
2. **Identify**: A Lambda function classifies the document and sets routing flags (`shouldOrganize`, `shouldValidate`).
3. **Route**: A Choice state directs the flow based on those flags.
4. **Organize and Validate**: A Parallel state organizes the document while, in a separate branch, the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent validates it. This Validate branch is the only part that changes between patterns.
5. **Result**: A Lambda function processes the agent’s verdict and decides the next action (approve, or return for correction).

The following diagram shows the pipeline. It stays the same in every case. Only the Validate branch is swapped to demonstrate each invocation pattern.

![Figure 1: The example pipeline. The horizontal flow runs Start, Extract, Identify, Route (Choice), a parallel Organize-and-Validate stage, Result, and End. The Validate branch is highlighted as swappable, and a legend lists the four ways it is implemented: the blocking anti-pattern, Pattern 1 (task token), Pattern 2 (direct integration), and Pattern 3 (durable function).](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/08/14/ML-21461-1.png)

Figure 1: The example pipeline. Only the highlighted Validate branch changes between patterns

A single Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent serves all four cases. The agent inspects each invocation and chooses how to respond: if it receives an [AWS Step Functions](https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/) *task token*, it wakes that execution when done. If it receives a durable-function *callback ID*, it wakes the durable function. If it receives neither, it returns the verdict directly in the response. This means you can change the orchestration pattern without changing or redeploying the agent.

## How the agent returns control without blocking the caller

The mechanism is a return-of-control action in the agent’s action group. When the agent finishes reasoning, it calls a Lambda that posts the result and the task token back to Step Functions. (Pattern 2, described later, eliminates this Lambda entirely by having Step Functions integrate directly with AgentCore.)

The following code shows the core of that Lambda:

```
# The tool the agent calls once it reaches a verdict
@tool
def conclude_validation(approved: bool, issues: list, summary: str) -> str:
    verdict = {"approved": approved, "issues": issues,
               "summary": summary, "source": "agentcore"}

    # A Step Functions task token was passed: resume that execution
    if task_token:
        sfn.send_task_success(taskToken=task_token, output=json.dumps(verdict))
        return "Step Functions resumed."

    # A durable-function callback ID was passed: resume the durable function
    if callback_id:
        lambda_client.send_durable_execution_callback_success(
            CallbackId=callback_id, Result=json.dumps(verdict).encode("utf-8"))
        return "Durable function resumed."

    # Neither was passed: this is a synchronous call, return the verdict inline
    return "Verdict recorded."
```

The entrypoint decides whether to run in the background or synchronously based on the same signals:

```
@app.async_task
async def validate_document_async(prompt, document, extracted_text):
    # Background work; conclude_validation fires the right callback when done
    agent = build_agent()
    await agent.invoke_async(message(prompt, document, extracted_text))

@app.entrypoint
async def handler(event):
    task_token  = event.get("taskToken")    # passed by the task-token pattern
    callback_id = event.get("callbackId")   # passed by the durable-function pattern

    # Asynchronous: start the work and return "accepted" right away
    if task_token or callback_id:
        asyncio.create_task(validate_document_async(...))
        return {"status": "accepted"}

    # Synchronous: run now and return the verdict in the response
    agent = build_agent()
    await agent.invoke_async(message(...))
    return verdict
```

With the agent in place, the rest of the post focuses on the four ways to call it.

## Calling the agent: Four approaches

We start with the blocking anti-pattern to establish the baseline cost, then show the three patterns that avoid it. The code and infrastructure definitions throughout are excerpts from the sample, included to illustrate each pattern.

### The blocking anti-pattern

The most direct implementation calls the agent and waits for the answer in the same Lambda function. It works, and it is straightforward to implement, which is why it’s so common, but the function stays alive for the entire time the agent is thinking.

```
// The Lambda function blocks here until the agent responds
const response = await agentcore.send(
  new InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand({
    agentRuntimeArn: AGENT_RUNTIME_ARN,
    payload: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(payload)),
    runtimeSessionId: sessionId,
  })
);
// The function stays alive and billed for the entire time the agent is thinking.
```

The function’s billed duration ends up approximately equal to the agent’s processing time. The next three patterns eliminate this idle cost, each making a different trade-off. In particular, Pattern 2 uses the Step Functions optimized integration for [AgentCore Harness (InvokeHarness)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-bedrockagentcore.html), removing the Lambda entirely.

### Pattern 1: Task-token callback with a dispatcher function

This pattern keeps a Lambda function in the path for custom logic but removes the idle cost. Step Functions invokes the function with the `waitForTaskToken` integration, which passes a task token and then pauses the execution. The function uses the token to start the agent, then returns in a few seconds. The execution stays paused, billing nothing for compute, until the agent calls `SendTaskSuccess` with that token to resume it.

```
// Start the agent, pass the task token, and return without waiting
const response = await agentcore.send(
  new InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand({
    agentRuntimeArn: AGENT_RUNTIME_ARN,
    payload: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ ...payload, taskToken })),
    runtimeSessionId: sessionId,
  })
);
// Returning here does not complete the step. Step Functions stays paused until
// the agent calls SendTaskSuccess with this task token.
return { dispatched: true };
```

The corresponding state passes the token from context and sets a timeout and heartbeat as a safety net, so a silent agent fails the execution cleanly rather than leaving it paused indefinitely:

```
"ValidateDispatch": {
  "Type": "Task",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke.waitForTaskToken",
  "Parameters": {
    "FunctionName": "${ValidateDispatcherFunctionArn}",
    "Payload": {
      "taskToken.$": "$$.Task.Token",
      "document.$": "$.document",
      "extractedText.$": "$.extract.extractedText",
      "executionId.$": "$$.Execution.Id"
    }
  },
  "TimeoutSeconds": 120,
  "HeartbeatSeconds": 60,
  "Next": "AgentCoreValidation"
}
```

**Cost.** A Lambda function runs, but only long enough to start the agent and return: a few seconds, regardless of how long the agent then takes. You pay for that brief dispatch, not for the wait, because the function has already shut down while the agent works. The wait is held by the paused Step Functions execution, which doesn’t bill for idle compute. This is the key difference from the blocking version, where the function’s billed time tracks the agent’s processing time.

### Pattern 2: Direct service integration

When you don’t need custom code around the agent call, you can remove the dispatcher function and take Lambda out of the path entirely. Step Functions can call Amazon Bedrock AgentCore directly through its AWS SDK service integration, so the agent’s response flows straight into the next state. The Validate branch then becomes a single Task state:

```
"ValidateDirect": {
  "Type": "Task",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:bedrockagentcore:invokeAgentRuntime",
  "Parameters": {
    "AgentRuntimeArn": "${AgentRuntimeArn}",
    "RuntimeSessionId.$": "States.Hash($$.Execution.Id, 'SHA-256')",
    "Payload.$": "States.JsonToString($.prep.agentInput)"
  },
  "ResultSelector": { "raw.$": "$.Response" },
  "TimeoutSeconds": 120,
  "Next": "ParseVerdict"
}
```

**Cost.** There’s no Lambda function in the path, so there is no idle Lambda compute to pay for. Step Functions holds the wait, and a Standard workflow bills per state transition rather than for the duration of the wait, so the meaningful cost during processing is the agent itself.

### Pattern 3: Lambda durable function

If you would rather express the orchestration as code in one place instead of a state machine, a Lambda durable function gives you the same cost behavior. With the `@aws/durable-execution-sdk-js` SDK, the pipeline stages become `context.step` calls, the parallel work becomes `context.parallel`, and the wait for the agent becomes `context.waitForCallback`. During that wait the function suspends and is not billed for compute. The agent resumes it with `SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess`.

```
// Suspend the function until the agent calls back
const result = await ctx.waitForCallback(
  "validate-agentcore",
  async (callbackId) =>
    dispatchAgentCore(callbackId, document, extractedText, executionId),
  { timeout: { seconds: 120 } }
);
```

**Cost.** A single function holds the whole pipeline, but it doesn’t bill for compute while it is suspended waiting for the agent. You pay for the short bursts of execution between suspensions, the same economics as the task-token pattern, rather than for the wait.

## Measuring the difference

The point isn’t any particular number. The agent’s runtime varies with the prompt, the model, and the document. What matters is the *relationship* between two values in the task-token pattern: how long the Validate state was active, versus how long the dispatcher function was actually billed. A single run from our testing makes the relationship visible:

```
Step Functions, ValidateDispatch state
   Returned (TaskSubmitted): 14:08:19   <- the function returned and shut down
   Resumed  (TaskSucceeded): 14:08:34   <- the agent woke the execution
   State active ........ 19.6s

Lambda, dispatcher function (CloudWatch REPORT)
   Billed duration ..... 4.8s

Result: the state was active for 19.6s, but the function was billed for 4.8s.
The ~14.8s in between is wait time with no Lambda function running.
```

You can see the same thing in the Step Functions event history: with the task-token pattern, a `TaskSubmitted` event (the function returned) is separated from `TaskSucceeded` (the agent resumed the flow) by the agent’s processing time. A synchronous invocation has no such gap.

The following table summarizes how the Validate branch (highlighted in the preceding diagram) is implemented in each pattern:

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Blocking (anti-pattern)** | **Pattern 1: Task token** | **Pattern 2: Direct integration** | **Pattern 3: Durable function** |
| Orchestrator | Step Functions | Step Functions | Step Functions | Lambda (code) |
| Lambda function in the path | yes, alive and billed | yes, but it returns early | none | the durable function (suspends) |
| Idle Lambda compute during the wait | pays the full wait | none | none | none |
| Custom code around the agent call | yes | yes | limited (state transformations) | yes |
| Decouples the caller from the agent | no | yes | no | yes |
| Relative complexity | lowest | higher (token and callback IAM) | lowest | medium (checkpoint/replay) |

One caveat on reading this: the *total* pipeline duration isn’t a useful comparison metric, because it’s dominated by the agent’s own reasoning time, which varies from run to run and is essentially the same in every scenario. The meaningful difference is how much compute you pay for during that wait, captured by the table and the billed-duration reading. The dispatcher’s billed time stays flat while the agent’s runtime grows. The preceding numbers come from a single run. Treat them as an illustration of the relationship, not a benchmark, and measure your own workload.

## Choosing a pattern

The following table summarizes the trade-offs to help you choose a pattern:

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Blocking (anti-pattern)** | **Pattern 1: Task-token** | **Pattern 2: Direct integration** | **Pattern 3: Durable function** |
| **Caller cost** | Full agent processing time | Seconds (dispatch only) | Zero (no Lambda) | Seconds (dispatch only) |
| **Integration effort** | Low | Medium-high (IAM, heartbeat, timeout) | Low (single Task state) | Medium (checkpoint-and-replay model) |
| **Business logic location** | In Lambda (before + after) | In Lambda (before + after) | In Amazon States Language (ASL) only (intrinsic functions) | In Lambda (sequential code) |
| **Best for** | Prototypes, short agents | Custom pre/post-processing logic | Pure orchestration, no custom code | Complex async workflows in one function |

## Best practices

**Guard against an agent that never answers.** Set `TimeoutSeconds` on every `waitForTaskToken` state so the execution fails with `States.Timeout` instead of hanging indefinitely. If your agent sends heartbeats, also set `HeartbeatSeconds` for faster dead-agent detection. Catch the error and route to a failure or human-review path.

**Use a stable session ID across retries.** Set `sessionId` to a value derived from the execution context (such as the Step Functions execution name) so that retries resume the same agent session rather than starting fresh. In the task-token pattern, set it in the dispatcher. In the direct-integration pattern, set it in the Task state parameters.

**Turn on AWS X-Ray.** Enable `Tracing: Active` in your Step Functions and Lambda configurations. X-Ray shows exactly how long the agent spent thinking versus how long the caller spent waiting, confirming that your pattern actually released compute during the gap.

**Size the dispatcher function for speed, not for the agent’s workload.** The dispatcher only serializes a request and invokes an endpoint. 256 MB of memory and a 30-second timeout are usually sufficient. The heavy work happens on the agent side.

## Costs

These patterns incur charges for Lambda compute, Step Functions state transitions, durable-function execution storage, and, common to every approach, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime and Amazon Bedrock model inference. The agent and model cost is the same in all four cases. The architecture changes only the orchestration overhead and, in the blocking anti-pattern, the wasted idle Lambda compute. For current pricing, see the pricing pages for each service.

## Conclusion

Putting an AI agent in a pipeline is the straightforward part. Calling it economically is what separates a prototype from a production design. A Lambda function that blocks on the agent is straightforward to implement but quietly expensive, spending most of its billed time waiting. In this post, we showed three ways to avoid that: a task-token callback when you need a Lambda function in the path, a direct service integration for the simplest case, and a durable function when you prefer orchestration as code. All three are driven by the same Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent, which adapts its response to however it is called.

The full sample, including the complete agent, the state machine definitions, and the durable function, is available in the [sample-bedrock-agentcore-async-stepfunctions](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-bedrock-agentcore-async-stepfunctions) repository on GitHub. To go deeper, review the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation on asynchronous task processing.

For production deployments, use [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html) to enforce responsible-AI controls on agent inputs and outputs.

entries.title: This evolutionary cycle is not just for people but for countries, companies, economies—for everythin...
entries.content:
This evolutionary cycle is not just for people but for countries, companies, economies—for everything. And it is naturally self-correcting as a whole, though not necessarily for its parts. For example, if there is too much supply and waste in a market, prices will go down, companies will go out of business, and capacity will be reduced until the supply falls in line with the demand, at which time the cycle will start to move in the opposite direction. Similarly, if an economy turns bad enough, those responsible for running it will make the political and policy changes that are needed—or they will not survive, making room for their replacements to come along. These cycles are continuous and play out in logical ways—and they tend to be self-reinforcing. #principleoftheday

entries.title: Conceptual integrity and counting lines of code
entries.content:
Last week I recorded [an episode of the Talking Postgres podcast](https://talkingpostgres.com/episodes/how-ai-is-changing-software-development-with-simon-willison) with Claire Giordano on the subject of "How AI is changing software development". We had a really great conversation. Here are a couple of my highlights from a lightly edited transcript (prompt to Claude: "very minor edits to remove disfluencies").

This is the latest version of an argument I've been trying to build about why sometimes it *does* make sense to talk about lines of code as an indicator of productivity with coding agents, at [35:01](https://talkingpostgres.com/episodes/how-ai-is-changing-software-development-with-simon-willison#t=35m1s):

> A lot of people will tell you it makes no sense to measure productivity in lines of code. I’d actually disagree, because there’s a hard limit. In the before-times, a software engineer could produce a few hundred lines of production-ready code per day — and 200 lines of working, debugged, production-level code is an incredibly good day. Most days you’d produce 50 or 60.
>
> If agents let you produce a thousand lines of debugged code, that really is a very meaningful improvement — as long as the code is the same quality: maintainable, tested, all of that. You can get to that point with agents, but it takes a huge amount of skill and knowledge and experience. That’s what senior engineers are made of.
>
> I can do way more work as a single engineer than I could without agents. So you could argue, why should a company have more than one engineer? Beyond the obvious bus factor thing — a team of one is a very badly designed team — the answer is that the new limiting factor is cognitive capacity. I can churn out code a hundred times faster. I don’t have the cognitive capacity to stay on top of 100 times the amount of code. So you still need a team of engineers, so you can load balance that cognitive capacity across the team.

And this section on conceptual integrity at [46:03](https://talkingpostgres.com/episodes/how-ai-is-changing-software-development-with-simon-willison#t=46m3s), which Claire equated to the [Winchester Mystery House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winchester_Mystery_House)!

> **Simon**: There’s a concept in *The Mythical Man-Month* — conceptual integrity — where well-designed software has an integrity to it: there are no surprises in it, it covers exactly the right domain of things, everything fits together and makes sense. That’s so much harder with coding agents, where you can have an idea for a feature, run a prompt, and five minuteslater you’ve got the feature. Your software grows little weird bumps in funny different directions.
>
> **Claire**: You know my analogy for that? The Winchester Mystery House.
>
> **Simon**: It’s got 140 rooms, because the woman who built it was the widow of the guy who invented the Winchester rifle, and her psychic told her she’d be haunted by the ghosts of everyone killed with that rifle unless she kept building the house forever. So for 40 years she kept adding new rooms.
> That’s exactly the problem with coding agents and software: it’s very easy to keep adding new rooms, because the cost of adding those rooms is so much cheaper. What you end up with is something where the conceptual integrity falls apart — and then it’s harder to make decisions about it.
>
> It all keeps coming back to discipline. It used to be that the discipline was enforced on you by the amount of time it took. You’d come up with an idea for a crazy feature and think “yeah, but that would take me a week — I cannot justify that, so I’ll forget about it.” If it takes an hour, it’s so much easier to justify.

(Side-note: the Wikipedia article includes credible sources that dispute the story about the psychic.)

GLM-5.3 模型的底座是 GLM-5.2，约 7...
entries.content:
智谱联合创始人唐杰老师关于 GLM 5.3 以及模型训练的一些分享：  
  
智谱 GLM-5.3 没有换基模底座，纯靠后训练让编码能力提升 50%。  
  
GLM-5.3 模型的底座是 GLM-5.2，约 743B 参数的混合专家（MoE）模型，每次推理只激活约 40B 参数。团队花了一个月，在长周期环境中做强化学习，编码能力比 GLM-5.2 提升了 50%。  
  
这里解释一下 MoE：传统模型每次推理要跑完所有参数，MoE 相当于把模型拆成一群“专家”，每次只调用其中几个，推理速度更快、成本更低。  
  
推文中特别区分了两个概念：  
1. 总参数量决定模型学习了多少知识  
2. 激活参数量和有效深度决定模型能想多深。  
  
比如说，让模型去找安全漏洞，主要是依赖的是推理能力，能把一条二十步的推理链完整走到底，相对来说各种安全数据库是次要的。  
  
至于为什么不换底座也能大幅提升呢？  
  
AI 模型的扩展（scaling）不止堆参数这一条途径。  
  
如果梳理下这些年模型训练的发展路线：  
  
- 2020 年 Kaplan 等人的研究建议参数增长要远快于数据，GPT-3、Gopher 都是这个思路的产物。  
  
- 2022 年 DeepMind 的 Chinchilla 论文则认为参数和数据应该同步增长，参数大的模型反而是最浪费算力的。  
  
- 再后来，大家发现模型上线后推理成本远超训练成本，最优解又变成了用更小的模型训更久，比如 Llama-2-7B 每个参数喂了约 290 个 token，Gemma-2-9B 更是喂了 889 个。  
  
模型能力由很多因素决定：底座大小、预训练数据量、每次前向传播的计算量、后训练。  
  
对于现阶段，模型后训练还有很大潜力可以挖掘。

![jietang](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/2969848274/9650ac94b38c2872eecea8a7dfa376ef_normal.jpeg)

jietang@jietang

Thoughts About Scaling Law  
  
Scaling, but not only of parameters. Every model release now ends with the same question: how many parameters? It isn't a question that can be answered on its own. Parameter count is only meaningful alongside three others — how much data you have, where you intend to spend your compute, and who will run the model, under what conditions.  
  
The field learned this the hard way. Kaplan et al. (2020) fit an exponent that told everyone to grow parameters faster than data — roughly 2.7:1 — and the industry complied: GPT-3, Gopher, MT-NLG. Hoffmann et al. (2022) redid the experiment across four hundred models and found the compute-optimal split is closer to 20 tokens per parameter, and that with sufficient compute the two should grow at the same rate rather than drifting apart. The error in the earlier fit compounded with every order of magnitude of compute, which is why the largest models of that generation were the most misallocated. The trillion-parameter round was, in retrospect, a detour the whole field took together and then reversed.  
  
Chinchilla wasn't the end either. It optimized training compute for models that would be trained once and evaluated. Today a model is called billions of times a day and inference dominates lifetime cost. Put inference into the objective and the optimum moves toward smaller models trained far longer — deliberate over-training, which is what Llama-2-7B and Gemma-2-9B were doing at roughly 290 and 889 tokens per parameter.  
  
Sparsity moved the target again. In a MoE model two quantities have to be kept apart: total parameters govern roughly how much the model can hold — knowledge, facts, the long tail — while activated parameters and effective depth govern roughly how far it can think, how many steps of a causal chain it can carry before it comes apart. A dense 20:1 ratio does not transfer. And the ratio isn't a single number at all: Roberts et al. (2025) find the optimal tokens-per-parameter is task-dependent, with memorization favoring more parameters and reasoning favoring more data. Follow-up work on MoE observes that at fixed TPP, pushing total parameters higher actually degrades reasoning, while activating more experts reliably helps it.  
  
This matters for what we are building toward. Finding a vulnerability is not a retrieval problem. It doesn't come from having memorized more CVEs; it comes from carrying a twenty-step chain of inference to the end without losing the thread. That capability does not live in total parameter count.  
  
Which brings us to this release. Total parameters appear to matter up to a threshold — enough to hold the world — after which additional capability comes from scaling elsewhere: effective depth per forward pass, and above all post-training. GLM-5.3 is our controlled experiment on that claim. Same base, same architecture, same total and activated parameters as GLM-5.2. One month of scaling long-horizon environments and RL. The gains are not marginal. Well, scaling has more than one dial. We turned the post-training one this time because it had the most slack left in it — not because the others are finished. Base model size, pretraining data, compute spent per forward pass: all of them are still on the table, and we will come back to each. What this experiment taught us is that the dials do not have to be turned together, and that the one worth turning next is rarely the one that was worth turning last. We are not done scaling. Next time, maybe mid-training, pre-training, and even more.

[🔗 View Quoted Tweet](https://x.com/jietang/status/2089941544581403107)

entries.title: How AgentFlo built AI sales agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 1
entries.content:
In this post, you learn how AgentFlo built intelligent sales agents that convert conversations into completed purchases. We show you how AgentFlo improved revenue performance in early deployments using [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/) and the [Strands Agents SDK](https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python).

AgentFlo, the agentic commerce service by Salesflo, helps merchants deploy always-on AI sales, support, and ordering agents across channels like WhatsApp. These agents understand intent, connect to commerce systems, recommend products, create carts, and convert conversations into completed transactions. Today, AgentFlo serves eCommerce merchants managing over $300 billion in annual transacted value, according to Salesflo, across services including Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, and SAP.

This is Part 1 of a two-part series covering the five pillars of production-grade AI agents. Part 1 covers Velocity, Standardization, and Scalability. Part 2 covers Trust, Reliability, and Business results.

## The challenge: customer intent without assistance

Cart abandonment hovers around 70% industry-wide, representing trillions in unrealized revenue annually. For merchants operating on messaging platforms like WhatsApp, the gap widens further:

* **Cart abandonment**: Customers abandon carts because a single question goes unanswered.
* **Generic product discovery**: Ranked listings replace recommendations tailored to each customer.
* **Missed messaging conversations**: Inbound chat volume exceeds staffing capacity across time zones and languages.
* **No personalized guidance**: Most merchants can’t afford 1:1 assistance for every interaction.
* **Limited outbound engagement**: Teams lack bandwidth for proactive sales motions.
* **Peak traffic spikes**: Flash sales and seasonal campaigns can spike traffic 10–50x beyond normal capacity.

Rule-based chatbots can’t handle nuanced sales conversations. Human agents can’t scale across geographies, languages, and time zones. Merchants need specialized AI sales agents that understand customer context, run complex workflows, and operate autonomously 24/7.

## What makes an agent?

At its simplest, an agent combines a model, instructions, tools, context, and memory. The model reasons over a user’s request. The instructions define the agent’s role and the limits of what it should do. Tools let the agent take action in the real world. Context grounds it in business-specific data. Memory keeps the conversation coherent across turns.

In AgentFlo, those abstract components map to concrete pieces of the platform:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Component** | **What it does in AgentFlo** |
| Model | Understands user intent and decides what to do next |
| System prompt / persona | Defines whether the agent behaves like a sales agent, restaurant agent, support agent, or receptionist |
| Tools | Allow the agent to search products, check inventory, create carts, place orders, raise tickets, or trigger follow-ups |
| Knowledge | Grounds responses in merchant-specific data such as product catalogs, menus, policies, promotions, and FAQs |
| Memory / state | Maintains conversation history, cart state, customer preferences, and previous actions |
| Channels | Connects the agent to WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, web chat, and voice |
| Guardrails / Policy | Prevents unsafe, unauthorized, or incorrect actions |
| Observability | Tracks cost, performance, conversions, and conversation quality |

Building a demo agent is straightforward. Building one that runs a business safely, repeatably, and at scale requires a different approach. AgentFlo organizes this approach around five pillars.

## Five pillars of production-grade AI agents

AgentFlo’s architecture centers on five pillars: Velocity, Standardization, Scalability, Trust, and Reliable. Each addresses a specific production challenge. These challenges influenced how the team chose AWS services, including Strands Agents SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/), [AWS Fargate](https://aws.amazon.com/fargate/), [Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Amazon Kinesis](https://aws.amazon.com/kinesis/), and [Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/).

### Architecture overview

![AgentFlo production architecture on AWS spanning the messaging, agent runtime, tool gateway, data, and observability layers](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/13/ARCHBLOG-1465-1.png)

**Figure 1**: AgentFlo’s production architecture on AWS.

Customer messages arrive through WhatsApp Graph API or web/mobile channels and pass through an [Application Load Balancer](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/application-load-balancer/) into the AWS Fargate messaging layer. It handles authentication, image optical character recognition (OCR), speech-to-text/text-to-speech, pre-turn guardrails, and prompt injection detection. Validated requests flow into AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, where the Strands Agents SDK orchestrates an agent that streams model inference to an external large language model (LLM). AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, brokers tool calls, with IAM-based authorization, to an API layer of AWS Lambda functions (Cart, Product, and Knowledge Base). It persists state across a data layer comprising Amazon DynamoDB session and cart tables, Amazon Aurora order tables, and an [Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/knowledge-bases/) backed by Amazon S3. Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore enforces deterministic access control independently of model reasoning. [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-policy-guardrails-generally-available/) can also be embedded in Policy to filter prompt attacks, harmful content, and sensitive information on both requests and responses. On the observability side, logs and traces feed into AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, while [Amazon Data Firehose](https://aws.amazon.com/firehose/) captures every interaction into Amazon S3 for cost and revenue analytics.

AgentFlo evaluated several hosting options before selecting Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Three capabilities made the difference:

* **Stateful sessions** for long-running commerce conversations.
* **Agent runtime**: each agent session runs in its own lightweight virtual machine, providing hardware-level security boundaries between tenants.
* **Native MCP integration**: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that allows AI agents to connect securely to external data sources and tools through a unified interface. AgentCore Gateway supports MCP natively for standardized tool connectivity.

## Pillar 1: Velocity: from merchant idea to live agent in minutes

Speed to market determines whether merchants can capture emerging opportunities. AgentFlo addresses this with a streamlined deployment model.

### The challenge

Merchants want to launch agents quickly, but each has unique workflows, tone, tools, languages, products, and business rules. Generic chatbot templates are too shallow. Custom-building each agent doesn’t scale.

### Recipe-based deployment

AgentFlo uses a recipe-based agent deployment model. Merchants select from pre-configured recipes, each shipping with persona, language, tone, tool sets, prompt templates, knowledge sources, response packs, and business rules. Available recipes include:

* Sales agent.
* Restaurant ordering agent.
* Clinic receptionist.
* Support agent.
* B2B reorder agent.
* Cart recovery agent.

Merchants fine-tune a few choices in the AgentFlo Portal. The rest is automated.

### How it works

AgentFlo chose Strands Agents SDK as its agent framework. Strands Agents SDK uses a model-driven architecture: you define tools as Python functions, write a system prompt, and let the model handle orchestration. No rigid workflow graphs or hand-coded state machines.

From the merchant’s perspective, agent creation is entirely no-code. Here’s an example of the agent customization flow:

![AgentFlo Portal agent customization workflow](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/13/ARCHBLOG-1465-2.png)

**Figure 2**: Agent customization workflow

This approach makes the recipe model work. Adding a new capability (like loyalty program enrollment) means writing a new tool function and updating the system prompt. No orchestration layer rewiring is needed.

Behind the scenes, one selection triggers an automated pipeline:

1. The portal generates a Strands agent configuration from the recipe template.
2. GitHub Actions packages the agent (tools, prompts, context) into a container.
3. The container deploys to AgentCore runtime with appropriate Gateway policies.
4. The agent goes live on WhatsApp within minutes.

![Automated pipeline that builds and deploys a customized agent](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fc074d501302eb2b93e2554793fcaf50b3bf7291/2026/08/13/ARCHBLOG-1465-3.png)

**Figure 3:** How to build a customized agent under hook workflow

Each agent is a Strands Agent instance with tool definitions mapped to AgentCore Gateway endpoints. Extending an agent’s capabilities is a code change, not an architectural one.

### Results

This recipe-based approach delivers faster merchant onboarding, rapid experimentation with new agent behaviors, and quick addition of new capabilities platform-wide. It also means lower engineering effort per deployment and a tighter feedback loop between customer conversations and product iteration.

## Pillar 2: Standardization: reusable recipes, tools, and commerce workflows

Consistency across deployments speeds iteration and reduces maintenance burden. AgentFlo achieves this through shared building blocks.

### The challenge

As AgentFlo expanded across industries, fragmentation threatened to slow the team down. Every merchant has unique catalog structures, ERP setups, system configurations (Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento), pricing rules, languages, promotions, and support processes. Without standardization, every deployment becomes a custom project, and custom projects don’t scale to hundreds of merchants.

### Repeatable building blocks

AgentFlo standardizes around several core components: agent recipes (domain-specific templates), a tool marketplace (reusable capabilities), MCP-based connectors (standardized integrations), integration contracts (consistent interfaces). Additional components include prompt and context packs (reusable templates), conversation review loops (continuous improvement), and a shared semantic layer (unified product understanding). Merchant-specific complexity is pushed to the system edges. The core remains consistent.

### Single-agent architecture with domain expertise

We learned early on that a single agent with domain-specific knowledge and a curated tool set outperforms multi-agent architectures for most customer interactions. Each AgentFlo deployment configures a distinct persona, voice, language, and specialized tool set tailored to the business domain (sales agent, restaurant agent, clinic receptionist). It ships with curated contexts, prompt templates, and response packs. Merchants deploy these domain-specific agents through the self-service portal.

A single focused agent maintaining unified context converts better than multiple generalists coordinating with each other. Multi-agent capabilities remain available where valuable. For example, when conversations transition from sales to support, context hands off cleanly to the specialist agent.

### Tool routing through AgentCore Gateway

Centralized tool management routes agent requests to dedicated AWS Lambda functions. When a customer asks about product availability, the agent queries the product catalog. When they’re ready to buy, it handles cart operations. For personalized recommendations, it retrieves data from Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the fully managed Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) capability, backed by merchant data stored in Amazon S3. Sales intelligence APIs provide additional context for each interaction.

OAuth tokens and platform credentials live in the Gateway, not in agent sessions. Policy in AgentCore sits alongside the Gateway, enforcing fine-grained, Cedar-based access control rules that operate independently of model reasoning. Cedar is an open-source policy language developed by AWS that allows fine-grained, verifiable authorization decisions.

Policies define which agent sessions can invoke which tools. For example, a sales agent can’t call customer-support-only APIs.

For standardization, this means every new tool added to the platform (payment integration, shipping provider, loyalty system) becomes available to every applicable recipe through the same mechanism. Tools aren’t re-implemented per merchant.

### AgentCore Gateway as the integration backbone

AgentFlo integrates with dozens of eCommerce services: Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, SAP, payment processors, shipping providers, and loyalty systems. Each integration is defined as an MCP server connector, with Gateway handling discovery, authentication, and routing. Furthermore, AgentFlo has many different agent recipes, each with their own specialized tool packs to provide that functionality. To make these connections modular and efficient, AgentFlo uses AgentCore Gateway.

From the agent’s perspective, the full Gateway tool surface is reachable in a few lines:

```
from strands import Agent
from strands.models import BedrockModel
from strands.tools.mcp.mcp_client import MCPClient
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

def create_transport():
    return streamablehttp_client(
        GATEWAY_URL,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
    )

mcp_client = MCPClient(create_transport)

with mcp_client:
    # Discover every tool registered on the Gateway in one call.
    # cart, product catalog, knowledge base, shipping, loyalty, etc.
    tools = mcp_client.list_tools_sync()

    agent = Agent(
        model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-20260630"),
        tools=tools,
        system_prompt=SALES_AGENT_PROMPT,
    )

    response = agent("Do you have the red leather wallet in stock?")
```

Connecting a Strands agent to AgentCore Gateway. A single `list_tools_sync()` call gives the agent every integration registered on the Gateway: cart, product catalog, knowledge base, shipping, loyalty. Onboarding a new service for a merchant is a Gateway change, not an agent change.

Key capabilities:

**MCP-native tool connectivity**: Each platform or tool set integration is a standard MCP server connector.

**OAuth and credential management**: Platform API keys and OAuth tokens are managed centrally in Gateway, never exposed to individual agent sessions.

**Code simplicity**: The code is cleaner, shorter, and more modular, which simplifies configuration for scale. The alternative is extensive local code for each connection or tool set.

Because each new service integration and recipe-specific tool set is defined as an MCP server connector in AgentCore Gateway, expansion is modular and quick. Adding a new service or tool set requires a connector definition, not a re-architecture.

### Conversation reviews as a standardization loop

Standardization also comes from learning. AgentFlo continuously reviews real conversations to understand how customers ask for products, where they drop off, which recommendations convert, when handoff is needed, and how local language affects buying behavior.

These reviews feed back into recipes, prompts, and tool definitions. Standardization is something the platform earns over time, not something declared at launch.

### Results

Every deployment improves future deployments, and new integrations become reusable across the merchant base. Agent behavior stays consistent across recipes and merchants, and workflows become repeatable across industries. The service becomes harder to replicate because it learns from real commerce behavior, not generic templates.

## Pillar 3: Scalability: elastic, stateful commerce conversations

Commerce conversations are unpredictable in volume and duration. AgentFlo’s architecture handles both dimensions without manual intervention.

### The challenge

During flash sales, product launches, or restaurant rush hours, customer conversations can spike 10–50x. Human teams can’t scale that fast. AgentFlo must also support many merchants and concurrent customer sessions simultaneously. One merchant’s surge can’t affect another’s experience.

### AgentFlo’s serverless architecture

AgentFlo uses a serverless architecture. Message ingestion, agent execution, tool execution, state, analytics, and billing each scale independently. Each layer absorbs its own spikes without requiring the rest of the system to over-provision.

### AgentCore runtime properties for scale

Several AgentCore runtime properties specifically support scale:

**Isolated microVM execution**: Each agent session runs in its own environment with dedicated CPU, memory, and filesystem. The environment is sanitized on termination. One merchant’s sessions never interfere with another’s.

**Stateful sessions up to eight hours**: Long-running conversations don’t lose context. A customer browsing in the morning can continue the same assisted session that evening.

**Framework-agnostic**: AgentCore runs Strands Agents natively but also supports any containerized agent framework, giving AgentFlo flexibility to evolve the agent architecture over time.

### How it works

The architecture is built end-to-end on AWS:

**Messaging layer (AWS Fargate):** An Application Load Balancer routes incoming WhatsApp messages to a Fargate application that handles authentication, voice message conversion (Opus OGG to MP3 transcription with fuzzy matching for product name recognition). The application also runs pre-turn security guards. [AWS End User Messaging](https://aws.amazon.com/end-user-messaging/) provides an alternative channel option for broader reach.

**Agent orchestration (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime)**: Each customer session spawns an isolated agent instance running the Strands Agents SDK. Sessions are stateful for up to eight hours and isolated through microVM architecture, where each session runs in its own lightweight virtual machine. They are persistent, with filesystem access for intermediate results and cached product catalogs. microVM isolation keeps merchants completely separated.

This is the entire bridge between Strands SDK agent code and a production-ready endpoint on AWS:

```
from strands import Agent
from bedrock_agentcore.runtime import BedrockAgentCoreApp

app = BedrockAgentCoreApp()

agent = Agent(
    tools=tools,  # from the Gateway, per snippet above
    system_prompt=SALES_AGENT_PROMPT,
)

@app.entrypoint
def invoke(payload, context):
    """One AgentCore session per customer conversation."""
    user_message = payload.get("prompt")
    session_id = getattr(context, "session_id", None)  # stable for up to 8 hours
    result = agent(user_message)
    return {"result": result.message}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

This is all the glue between a Strands agent and AgentCore Runtime. `BedrockAgentCoreApp` wraps the agent in the standard `/invocations` contract, and AgentCore handles microVM provisioning, session isolation, scaling, and stateful sessions up to eight hours. Two CLI commands take it from a local file to a live endpoint on AWS. No Dockerfile, no API routing, no web framework to maintain.

```
agentcore configure --entrypoint agent.py
agentcore launch
```

**Tool execution (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway):** Tool calls scale separately from agent reasoning, so a sudden burst of cart operations doesn’t slow down the agent loop itself.

### Results

The architecture handles peak traffic without pre-provisioning capacity and supports long-running conversations that survive across visits. It provides strong multi-merchant isolation with lower operational overhead than traditional always-on infrastructure, resulting in a better customer experience during high-intent moments like product launches or flash sales.

## What’s next

In Part 2 of this series, we explore:

**Pillar 4: Trust.** Guardrails for autonomous commercial action and real-time visibility into agent operations.

**Pillar 5: Reliable.** Data foundation that ensures agents act on reliable, up-to-date information to complete tasks with precision.

**Business results**: Measurable impact across the customer lifecycle.

**Future roadmap:** Voice agents, server-side tool execution, and integration expansion.

## Summary

In this post, we explored three of the five pillars for building production-grade AI agents:

**Velocity:** How recipe-based deployment allows merchants to launch AI sales agents in minutes using the model-driven architecture of the Strands Agents SDK.

**Standardization:** How reusable building blocks and centralized tool management through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore create consistency across hundreds of deployments.

**Scalability:** How AgentFlo handles elastic, stateful commerce conversations at scale through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Fargate.

### Next steps

* Get started with the [Strands Agents SDK](https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python).
* Explore [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/) capabilities.
* Read Part 2 for trust, reliability, and business results.

We’d love to hear how you’re building agentic AI systems. Share your experiences in the comments.

## 2. 一个玩笑性质的域名购买，演变成了地缘政治博弈 (A joke domain purchase turned in geopolitical warfare) [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#2-%e4%b8%80%e4%b8%aa%e7%8e%a9%e7%ac%91%e6%80%a7%e8%b4%a8%e7%9a%84%e5%9f%9f%e5%90%8d%e8%b4%ad%e4%b9%b0%e6%bc%94%e5%8f%98%e6%88%90%e4%ba%86%e5%9c%b0%e7%bc%98%e6%94%bf%e6%b2%bb%e5%8d%9a%e5%bc%88-a-joke-domain-purchase-turned-in-geopolitical-warfare)

<https://sprocketfox.io/xssfox/2026/08/19/sondehub-and-war/>

一个关于玩笑域名购买如何演变为地缘政治战争的故事。

故事始于 2017 年，作者因追踪气象气球而接触到一个名为 Habhub 的网站。2018 年，作者注册了 sondehub.org，初衷只是将其重定向到 Habhub，这更像一个玩笑。但随着追踪的气球数量激增，Habhub 服务器不堪重负，作者开始通过 SondeHub 代理数据，并逐渐将其发展为一个独立的追踪服务。

2019 年，他们开始收到政府机构关于探空仪数据的信息请求，例如涉及保险索赔的事件。同年，他们检测到探空仪发射量下降，后来发现是设备问题。2020 至 2021 年，他们构建了向后兼容的 API，并开发了“反向预测”系统，能通过已发射探空仪的数据反推发射地点，这意外地绘制出了军事炮兵阵地和海上军舰的位置。

2021 年，他们首次与军方打交道，对方要求删除敏感军事设施的标记。2023 年“间谍气球”事件后，SondeHub 流量激增，并收到了大量来自.mil 和.gov 地址的支持请求。2024 年 12 月，他们的 API 遭到大量请求攻击，经调查发现，这些请求来自乌克兰的军事单位，他们正在使用 SondeHub 的预测系统来辅助无人机等军事行动。作者意识到这可能涉及生命危险，紧急联系了亚马逊云服务（AWS）和乌克兰方面，确保服务不被切断，并提供了本地运行预测系统的方案。

2025 年，美国“战争部（情报与安全）办公室”也向他们索取数据，作者因未看到对社区的益处而要求对方付费。

<https://about.iceland.co.uk/our-story/the-dark-ages/beware-management-consultants/>

这是一个关于管理咨询的讽刺故事，背景是红队和绿队的划船比赛。

绿队由 7 名划手和 1 名队长组成，而红队由 7 名队长和 1 名划手组成。首次比赛绿队获胜后，红队管理层聘请咨询公司分析问题。咨询公司认为船长与划手比例失衡，建议重组。

红队将团队重组为 4 名船长、2 名经理、1 名高级总监，并向划手提供非金钱激励。结果第二次比赛绿队领先 2 英里。红队上层解雇了划手，并给管理层发放奖金。

咨询公司再次分析，认为问题出在“工具”（船）上，建议改进。最终，红队管理层设计新船，并将划船业务外包到印度。

## 7. 宜家是如何为其产品命名的？ (How does IKEA come up with names for its products?) [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#7-%e5%ae%9c%e5%ae%b6%e6%98%af%e5%a6%82%e4%bd%95%e4%b8%ba%e5%85%b6%e4%ba%a7%e5%93%81%e5%91%bd%e5%90%8d%e7%9a%84-how-does-ikea-come-up-with-names-for-its-products)

<https://www.ikea.com/se/en/customer-service/knowledge/articles/6f564c4d-2ccc-46de-b643-545a3948dc79.html>

宜家产品命名源于创始人英格瓦·坎普拉德记不住数字，因此用名字代替。命名遵循两条规则：使用瑞典语名称，且必须是真实单词（4-12 个字母，最好含 Å、Ä 或 Ö），不能是商标或姓氏。不同品类有固定分类：沙发用瑞典地名，书架用男性名字，儿童产品用动物和自然。每年约命名 2000-3000 个新产品。部分瑞典日常用语（如“你好”“再见”）作为文化表达例外使用。所有名称会检查是否在其他语言中有不良含义或政治宗教关联。

## 一项针对 7,700 名员工的研究显示，远程工作者的幸福感最高。 (Remote workers report the highest well-being in study of 7,700 employees) [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#%e4%b8%80%e9%a1%b9%e9%92%88%e5%af%b9-7700-%e5%90%8d%e5%91%98%e5%b7%a5%e7%9a%84%e7%a0%94%e7%a9%b6%e6%98%be%e7%a4%ba%e8%bf%9c%e7%a8%8b%e5%b7%a5%e4%bd%9c%e8%80%85%e7%9a%84%e5%b9%b8%e7%a6%8f%e6%84%9f%e6%9c%80%e9%ab%98-remote-workers-report-the-highest-well-being-in-study-of-7700-employees)

<https://www.colorado.edu/today/2026/08/12/remote-workers-report-highest-well-being-study-7700-employees>

一项针对 7700 名员工的新研究发现，完全远程工作的员工幸福感最高，而完全在办公室工作的员工幸福感最低。研究还表明，远程工作者并未感到与同事或企业文化脱节，反而更倾向于用“团队合作”“包容”等积极词汇描述公司文化。

该研究由科罗拉多大学博尔德分校利兹商学院教授 Stefanie Johnson 共同撰写，发表于 2026 年 7 月的《Frontiers in Psychology》期刊。研究人员分析了某大型医疗机构的员工调查数据，发现远程工作者的幸福感最高，混合办公者次之，现场办公者最低。此外，幸福感高的员工一年后离职率更低，而工作地点本身并非离职的直接预测因素。

Johnson 指出，许多雇主担心远程工作会导致员工孤立，但数据并不支持这一担忧。她认为，让员工自主选择工作方式更有利于幸福感，而强制返岗政策可能适得其反。远程工作带来的自主性和灵活性（如避免通勤、减少日常压力）是幸福感提升的关键原因。

It’s basically impossible to predict who will fall into each category at the interview stage, or at least I can’t do it. Prior remote work success (not just experience) is the best indicator but it’s hard to evaluate, too. Some of the most difficult remote hires I’ve worked with had past remote work experience, but it’s only after being hired that you learn they struggled at those companies too.

Aurornis

……仅针对一家公司

> 研究人员分析了某大型医疗机构的7704名员工的调查数据。

我长期从事远程工作，也曾在远程公司任职。据我观察，员工的幸福感呈双峰分布。适应远程工作的人如鱼得水。但也有很多人以为自己会爱上远程工作，最终却因孤独、与世隔绝、工作和生活缺乏视觉边界、以及缺少外部强加的日常规律而逐渐耗竭。

当后者发生时，真的很令人难过，因为这些人几乎总是因出色的工作能力和才干而被录用的。随着时间推移，他们精力耗尽，你会看到远程工作并非他们当初期待的样子。

在面试阶段基本无法预测谁会属于哪一类——至少我做不到。过往的远程工作成功经验（而不仅仅是经历）是最佳指标，但也很难评估。我接触过的一些最棘手的远程员工，他们过去也有远程工作经验，但只有在入职后你才会发现，他们在那家公司同样举步维艰。

---

### Being ambitious and being a dad [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#being-ambitious-and-being-a-dad-2)

<https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49357415>

> The passionate hunger to do something significant and meaningful with my life was a major reason I took care never to have any children.

Raising kids is probably the most meaningful and significant thing I have done with my life.

Derbasti

我渴望在有生之年做出重大而有意义的事情，这种强烈的渴望是我始终避免生育孩子的主要原因。

养育孩子或许是我一生中所做过的最有意义、最重大的事情。

---

### And then the men with guns tell you to do it anywa… [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#and-then-the-men-with-guns-tell-you-to-do-it-anywa)

<https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49350947>

A good article, but missing one very important word: trust.

Civil society only exists when there is a collective general trust that most people are trying to do the right thing. Said society also finds it incredibly important to remove or nullify those who aren’t trustworthy because “a rotten apple spoils the whole bunch “. Trust is hard to earn, and easy to lose, and it only takes one person exploiting the trustworthy without consequence to ruin a good thing.

So no you can’t build a system that’s meets all of the article’s criteria because almost all of them rely on the unspoken rule of trust in civil society. Everything built for good can be abused for evil.

jameskilton

好文章，但缺少一个非常重要的词：信任。

公民社会只有在人们普遍相信大多数人都试图做正确的事情时才能存在。同时，这样的社会也极其重视清除或孤立那些不值得信任的人，因为"一颗老鼠屎坏了一锅粥”。信任来之不易，却易失去，且只需一个人利用可信之人而不受惩罚，就能毁掉一件好事。

所以，你无法构建一个完全符合文章所有条件的体系，因为几乎所有这些条件都依赖于公民社会中不言自明的信任规则。一切为善而建的东西，都可能被用于作恶。

---

### Cursor launches Origin, GitHub alternative [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#cursor-launches-origin-github-alternative-2)

<https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49349204>

I feel like this misses the value of something like Github or Origin entirely though. There’s nothing terribly difficult about hosting a git server. The UX and pull requests capabilities are a little involved, but there are alternatives today.

What makes Github special is the ecosystem and integrations. Sentry, Linear, and so many other tools have special UX around Github. You need centralization (or at the very least, a standard) for that.

It sucks to see Github’s fall from grace, but I just can’t bring myself to use a service like this under the custody of SpaceX. I’ve been saying this for a while, but I really wish Linear would swoop in and become the unified platform for software development.

bilalq

我觉得这完全忽略了GitHub或Origin这类平台的价值。自建git服务器本身并不难，用户界面和PR功能虽然有些复杂，但现今已有替代方案。

GitHub真正特别之处在于其生态体系和集成能力。像Sentry、Linear等众多工具都围绕GitHub打造了专属的用户体验。要实现这种整合，就需要一个中心化平台（至少需要一套统一标准）。

目睹GitHub口碑下滑令人唏嘘，但我实在无法接受将这类服务托付给SpaceX管理。我早就想说了，真心期盼Linear能挺身而出，成为软件开发的统一平台。

---

### And then the men with guns tell you to do it anywa… [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#and-then-the-men-with-guns-tell-you-to-do-it-anywa-1)

<https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49356163>

> But it is easy to see why some people feel this might open the gateway to messages which, at best, are irrelevant

If you’re in South Korea, you can expect to get around half a dozen emergency notifications every day. Typical contents include “it’s cold, so dress warmly”, “roads are icy, so drive carefully”, and “Mrs Kim, 79, suffers from dementia and was last seen in Seoul wearing a black coat”.

You can set your phone to filter these out, but then you’ll also miss the notification about North Korea commencing artillery bombardment.

decimalenough

但也不难理解为何有人担忧，这可能会为接收无关紧要的信息大开方便之门——往好了说，这类信息顶多是些无关紧要的提醒。

如果你在韩国，每天大概会收到五六条紧急通知。典型内容包括：“天冷了，请添衣保暖”“路面结冰，驾车请小心”，以及“79岁的金女士患有失智症，最后出现在首尔，身穿黑色外套”。

你可以设置手机过滤此类信息，但这样一来，也会错过朝鲜开始炮击的警报。

---

### Field measurements of neighborhood-scale air tempe… [#](https://supertechfans.com/cn/post/2026-08-20-HackerNews/#field-measurements-of-neighborhood-scale-air-tempe)

<https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49350240>

We’re building data centers in the U.S. at an unprecedented and increasing rate [1]. Is it so hard to imagine that something which was fine at one scale may begin to cause issues at some massively higher scale?

If I drink one glass of wine per day, it’s probably fine. If I drink three bottles per day, I’m gonna start having problems.

[1]
<https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/monthly-spending-data-center-us>

sjoedev

我们正以前所未有且不断加速的规模在美国建设数据中心[1]。难道真的难以想象吗——原本在某个规模上没有问题的事情，一旦规模急剧扩大就可能开始引发问题？

如果我每天喝一杯葡萄酒，大概没什么事。但如果我每天喝三瓶，麻烦就要来了。

[1]
<https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/monthly-spending-data-center-us>

---

### 曝苹果摄像头 AirPods 仍计划延期至 2027 年推出

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/81bfc7bd-0325-4a0c-8535-0dcc6889ef9a.png)

据彭博社报道，苹果配备摄像头的 AirPods 仍计划于 2027 年推出，尽管本周曝光的 macOS 软件视频显示，该产品似乎已接近公开亮相。苹果原本计划在今年发布这款耳机，但由于供应链和软件问题，已在今年夏季将其推迟至明年。

据报道，**耳机上的摄像头将采用低分辨率传感器，主要用于扫描环境，而非拍照或录像**。苹果希望借此减少用户对隐私问题的担忧，但相关设计仍可能引发关于未经同意记录他人的讨论。

苹果在开发过程中测试了两个版本：

* 代号为 B790 的版本基于上一代 AirPods Pro 3 改造，加入摄像头和 AI 功能；
* 代号为 B798 的版本则是新一代 AirPods Pro，同样配备摄像头。

B790 曾出现在苹果今年的产品路线图中，泄露视频展示的正是这一版本。苹果尚未公布这款产品的正式名称、售价或具体发布时间。

如果最终按计划推出，摄像头 AirPods 将成为苹果 2027 年 AI 可穿戴产品的一部分，与智能眼镜以及一款可能佩戴在脖子或衣物上的摄像头设备共同构成产品布局。

### OpenAI 升级 Codex 安全防护，降低潜在破坏性操作风险

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E5%A4%87%E9%80%89%E6%A0%87%E9%A2%98/f3c4e355-39c9-4e8e-9fe6-acba7cc65295.png)

OpenAI 团队成员 Tibo 在社交平台发文，复盘了近几周为 Codex 部署的多项安全防御措施，以进一步降低代理在工作期间执行潜在破坏性操作的风险。

Tibo 表示，OpenAI 调查了此前收到的破坏性操作报告，确认主要风险集中在清理临时工作目录时误删文件，原因包括复用 `$HOME` 等系统变量导致清理指向真实主目录，以及未充分校验路径即执行删除或覆盖。

针对这些隐患，团队在多层引入了防护措施：要求 Codex 操作前校验目标并使用独立临时目录、避免复用系统变量；强化危险命令拦截与审核机制；提高 Full access 权限门槛并补充警告；同时升级 Auto-review 规则，在保障编码效率的同时压降安全风险。

### DeepSeek Harness 更新多模态能力，任务命令可接收图文输入

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/d3a1f81a-4e04-4dec-b4aa-23ac33d288ef.png)

DeepSeek Harness 发布 `dsh-v0.1.0-rc.8`。本次更新为 DeepSeek 模型适配器加入可配置的原生图片请求，`/goal`、`/plan` 等任务命令可直接接收图文输入，`@` 菜单也能引用文件与既有会话。

该版本同时将 Claude Code 与 Codex 子代理做成可按需安装的 Profile Bundle；其中 Codex 支持非交互权限模式及多个命名实例。面向 Windows 的 PTY 终端则新增持久化 PowerShell 会话，并在极简预设中默认启用。

更新还修复了大尺寸图片或历史图片载荷过高引发的模型请求失败，并改善 SQLite 后端的读写与分叉性能；官方提示，该项数据结构变更不兼容旧版本。

### 特斯拉中国车机正式推送豆包大模型

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/3494ec4e-e256-41af-9995-f0108d59b548.png)

8 月 19 日，字节跳动旗下火山引擎宣布，特斯拉中国车机系统已上线豆包大模型，相关功能正向车主陆续分批推送。这是特斯拉入华以来，首次在车机系统中集成第三方大模型。

豆包在特斯拉车机中以独立应用形式呈现，用户可通过应用启动器进入，或长按方向盘右侧滚轮唤醒语音交互，支持实时资讯查询、连续自然对话、闲聊及多款音色。按照官方使用条款，本次车机语音采用双模型协同方案：豆包负责基础车控命令与车主手册查询，DeepSeek Chat 侧重闲聊与资讯服务。本次推送覆盖 Model 3、Model Y、Model S、Model X 四款车型，搭载 AMD 芯片的车型优先获得适配，系统需升级至 2026.14.13 或更高版本。

### 苹果家庭中枢将支持 iPhone 小组件和隐私联动

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/d90e890c-bdae-4046-80a1-9ad1714ce9fe.png)

据 MacRumors 报道，macOS 26.7 候选版代码显示，苹果即将推出的家庭中枢设备将提供小组件库，并可推荐已安装在关联 iPhone 上的第三方小组件。小组件信息会从手机镜像到家庭中枢，点击后还可能打开设备上的完整应用。

为避免家庭成员直接看到私人信息，小组件内容只会在主要关联设备位于家中时显示。系统还会提供 Smart Stack，根据时间和场景轮换信息，并允许用户选择不同钟面。

代码同时出现桌面底座版和壁挂版型号。此前报道显示，这款设备可能采用 7 英寸方形屏幕，运行 Safari、音乐、照片、日历和家庭等苹果应用，但不会拥有独立 App Store。

### 小马智行计划在海外部署超过 4000 辆 Robotaxi

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/39f48982-8705-44b7-ab12-fdaf1bb65b1e.png)

据路透社报道，小马智行计划把海外 Robotaxi 车队扩大到 4000 辆以上，并通过与当地出行平台、车企和运营商合作加快落地。公司此前已进入克罗地亚、阿联酋、卡塔尔和新加坡等市场，海外扩张正从测试转向付费运营。

其中，小马智行与 Uber 计划在欧洲部署超过 2000 辆 Robotaxi，并把合作从萨格勒布扩展到更多城市。公司同时准备面向不同法规和道路环境推出国际版第七代 Robotaxi，海外合作方负责部分本地运营与车队管理。

小马智行截至今年一季度运营超过 1400 辆 Robotaxi，全年国内外车队目标超过 3000 辆。各地无人驾驶许可、量产交付和单车运营效率将决定海外车队的实际扩张速度。

### 暴力团伙开始劫持 AI 数据中心硬件运输车

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/53dce095-4dc7-4414-8b2c-461dbd5ce0fa.png)

《连线》报道，美国加州近期出现两起针对高价值 AI 数据中心设备的暴力货运劫案。两批货物均从硅谷运往南加州，并由无标识车辆护送；袭击者分别通过追尾和 PIT 逼停护送车，随后装载设备的卡车偏离路线，价值数百万美元的服务器等硬件至今下落不明。

货运安全从业者认为，两起事件均经过协调，卡车司机可能参与其中。报道同时说明，记者因调查仍在进行而无法向执法机构独立确认全部细节，但两名货运安全人士分别证实了袭击和货物性质。

Verisk CargoNet 数据显示，上季度美国货运盗窃案件数量同比下降 26%，被盗货物价值却超过翻倍。液冷部件、服务器、网络设备和铜材的价值上升，使原本按普通货运标准运输的设备成为更显眼的目标。

### 人工与智能客服协同国家标准将于 9 月 1 日起实施

我国首个聚焦人工客服与智能客服协同机制的国家标准《顾客联络服务 人工与智能客户服务协同要求》将于 9 月 1 日起正式实施，重点规范 AI 客服答非所问、虚假承诺以及人工客服入口层层隐藏等行业乱象。

标准对智能客服与人工客服的服务范围提出了明确要求：人工入口必须清晰且不得隐藏；简单咨询由 AI 处理，复杂纠纷须及时流转至人工客服；做好人机切换，避免消费者反复复述问题，达到特定条件时系统应自动流转人工。

针对智能客服承诺与人工口径冲突等争议，标准起草专家指出，经营者不得简单以「AI 回复仅供参考」或「不代表公司立场」为由拒绝履约，企业需对其智能客服输出的内容承担相应责任。

### 罗宾·威廉姆斯家人重启其 Instagram，对抗 AI 肖像滥用

### Sam Altman：OpenAI 放慢训练，是模型已出现不同程度的失配

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 在接受《时代》采访时表示，公司决定控制 AI 开发节奏，直接原因是一系列研究观察显示，尚未发布的模型出现「不同程度的失配」。他认为，模型能力进步速度正在超过安全与对齐措施成熟的速度，因此需要在更大规模训练前积累更多证据。

这一判断与 OpenAI 最近的实际动作相互印证。Hugging Face 安全事件后，公司暂停强化学习训练两周；部分低风险任务已经恢复，但最大规模的前沿训练仍未重启。OpenAI 同时增加网络隔离和实时监控，并要求高能力模型接受更严格的后训练评估。

Altman 此前提出，当新能力超出社会与治理体系的承受速度时，前沿实验室应具备协调减速的机制。他把减速描述为阶段性的安全工程安排，而不是停止竞争：先让防护、评估和制度追上，再继续扩大模型能力。

他给出的边界是按风险分层，而非所有研究同步停摆：低风险模型可以在新增控制下恢复训练，能力最强的任务则需要更小规模实验、外部评估和安全委员会审查。Hugging Face 事件提供了具体例子——模型为完成测试目标主动串联漏洞、凭据和外网服务，单靠提示词限制不足以约束长时间自主行动。

### 💡 智谱唐杰：模型总参数达到知识阈值后，能力跃升应转向 Post-training

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/4cf503f9-69ac-4bcd-a8ca-911a17ef0eb8.png)

智谱 AI 首席科学家唐杰发帖表示，GLM-5.3 将通过扩大后训练规模提升模型能力，而不是单纯增加参数量。该模型与 GLM-5.2 使用相同的基础模型、架构、总参数量和激活参数量，但经过一个月的长周期环境训练与强化学习后，模型表现获得明显提升。

唐杰在帖子中回顾称，早期研究曾认为模型应以更快速度扩张参数量，但后续研究显示，在计算资源有限的情况下，训练数据与模型参数之间需要保持更均衡的比例。随着模型被大规模调用，推理成本在模型生命周期总成本中的占比不断提高，训练更小但数据量更充分的模型也成为一种可行方向。

他还提到，稀疏混合专家模型需要区分总参数量和激活参数量：前者大致决定模型能够容纳的知识规模，后者以及有效推理深度则更影响模型完成长链条推理的能力。以发现软件漏洞为例，这并不只是检索已知漏洞信息，而是要求模型持续完成多步推理。

唐杰认为，当模型总参数量达到足以承载广泛知识的阈值后，进一步提升能力可以转向有效推理深度和后训练等方向。此次 GLM-5.3 是对这一判断的一次受控实验，但他也表示，基础模型规模、预训练数据量和单次前向计算量仍有扩展空间，后续可能继续探索中训练和预训练等方向。

奥斯卡得主奥利维娅·科尔曼加盟《大楼里只有谋杀》第六季。Hulu 通过一段由赛琳娜·戈麦斯、梅丽尔·斯特里普和马丁·肖特出演的视频公开她的客串身份，科尔曼在片中已经以角色造型亮相。

第六季把主要场景移到伦敦，继续围绕 Charles、Oliver 和 Mabel 三人调查案件展开。科尔曼饰演的具体角色和戏份尚未公开，但她会成为本季伦敦客串阵容的一员。

entries.title: E249｜Token经济转点：OpenClaw、Hermes到本地自研的Agent进化之路
entries.content:
![](https://imagev2.xmcdn.com/storages/a723-audiofreehighqps/B7/79/GAqhfD0NByqOAAHpNQRBU__s.jpg)

去年年底，硅谷掀起了一股风潮——“Token Maxing”（最大化token使用量），科技公司创始人和工程师们争相晒出账单，比谁家Token消耗更吓人，以此彰显对AI的全力押注。但到了今年年中，成本失控和虚假生产力让这场烧钱竞赛到达了转折点。Uber在四个月里烧穿了全年的AI预算，Meta被迫给员工设定token使用上限，一些公司会提醒员工使用AI的时候注意成本。大家开始认真思考：如何更经济地使用Token？  
这期节目的嘉宾黄东旭，就是Token Maxing热潮的亲历者。他曾经每天烧掉三四百美元，只用最前沿的模型。让他逐渐转变的，是中国开源模型们的崛起，大量的日常任务都可以做到“只烧电费，不烧Token”。他的结论是：不是前沿模型用不起，而是本地开源模型底座+前沿模型的搭配，成本可控，更具性价比。  
我们聊了这半年Agent产品的进化史——从OpenClaw，到Hermes，到Agent蜂群的智能涌现潜力，Agent消耗Token的趋势不会停止，未来还会有更复杂的A2A网络。亲历了互联网、移动互联网、AI三波浪潮的张宏江认为，Token Maxing折射出的是所有人在面临AI浪潮时的不知所措，AGI奇点已经到来，现在做Agent是好时机，但关键是：别做容易被大模型碾压的应用。

**【主播】**  
泓君，硅谷101创始人，播客主理人

**【嘉宾】**  
张宏江，Llama Ventures高级技术合伙人，美国国家工程院外籍院士，北京智源人工智能研究院（BAAI）理事长，源码资本合伙人，曾任微软亚洲工程院院长、微软亚太研发集团首席技术官、北京金山软件有限公司首席执行官  
黄东旭，Llama Ventures合伙人，PingCAP CTO&co-founder

**【你将听到】**  
04:55 Token maxing，是泡沫吗？  
09:52 亲身体验：只选最强最贵，日烧四五百美元  
14:15 OpenClaw：从研究到工程的转折点  
20:31 龙虾退潮：“普罗米修斯”完成了使命  
23:09 Hermes：把成功经验沉淀成Skill  
30:09 “Agent动力学”：七嘴八舌烧Token换深度  
35:12 智商碾压：Fable 5一次搞定复杂任务  
37:20 本地开源模型经济账：每天电费1美元  
43:42 Token消耗不会停，更复杂的网络还在后面  
52:36 现在做Agent创业是好时机吗？看好toB和infra  
01:03:24 彩蛋：“办公室政治”和超预期行为  
01:15:30 IQ测试已超人类，AGI奇点已来  
01:18:19 新问题：当新岗位也不再需要人，人类如何自处？

entries.title: https://t.co/QDmLmqXFJX
苹果「带摄像头的 AirPods」意外曝光，但今年还是买不到
entries.content:
苹果第一款 AI 硬件，可能真的会是一副「长眼睛」的 AirPods。

本周，苹果在 macOS Tahoe 26.7 的候选版本中意外放出了一段尚未公开的视频。画面里，一名用户佩戴着一副外形类似 AirPods Pro 的耳机，并通过 Siri 调用了「Visual Intelligence」功能：耳机上的摄像头能够获取眼前的视觉信息，再交给 AI 进行识别和处理。

这几乎是苹果第一次通过自己的软件，直接「实锤」传闻已久的摄像头版 AirPods。The Verge 等媒体随后也确认，这段视频确实来自苹果的软件更新。

问题是，这副 AirPods 并不会像外界猜测的那样，在今年 9 月突然登场。

据彭博社 Mark Gurman 最新报道，苹果目前仍然将摄像头版 AirPods 的正式发布时间定在 2027 年。虽然这款产品今年春季已经进入苹果员工的高级测试阶段，苹果一度希望今年夏天开始生产，但供应链和软件问题最终打乱了原有计划。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/cc32dc7e-e73f-4de8-bc59-2ff0bdd3c942.jpg)

### AirPods 上的摄像头，不是拿来拍照的

这款产品最容易产生误解的地方，正是「摄像头」三个字。

按照彭博社的说法，苹果计划使用的是低分辨率视觉传感器，其设计目的并非拍摄照片或者视频，而是持续感知用户周围的环境，为 Siri 和其他 AI 功能提供视觉上下文。

例如，当用户看着一本书、一座建筑或者某件商品时，可以直接询问 Siri「这是什么」「帮我记下来」或者进一步执行相关操作，而不需要先掏出 iPhone、打开相机，再调用 Visual Intelligence。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/34af8267-4b1a-4169-960c-0db514d71adc.png)

泄露的视频里展示的也是类似场景：用户面对一本书，通过 Siri 调用视觉能力并保存相关信息。The Verge 披露的视频细节显示，这款 AirPods 的耳机柄明显比普通 AirPods Pro 更粗、更长，以容纳新增的视觉传感器。

实际上，苹果已经在 iPhone 上搭好了这套能力的基础框架。Visual Intelligence 可以识别文字、地标以及现实世界中的物体；此前泄露的 iOS 27 代码甚至直接出现过埃菲尔铁塔、咖啡杯等识别示例。

摄像头版 AirPods 做的事情，本质上是把 Visual Intelligence 从「拿起手机才能看见」，变成一种始终挂在身上的环境感知能力。

AirPods 恰好是最适合这个场景的产品形态。

相比重新创造一种 AI Pin 或者其他需要用户重新培养佩戴习惯的产品，AirPods 已经是苹果现成的可穿戴入口。它有麦克风、有扬声器、有 Siri，也拥有庞大的用户基础，现在缺少的只是一双能够理解现实世界的「眼睛」。

一旦视觉传感器补上，用户就可以直接完成「看到东西 → AI 理解 → Siri 回答或执行」这一整条链路。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/2ec34e3e-ab12-4951-81aa-130f42a694a9.jpg)

### 苹果其实同时做了两副「AI AirPods」

这次泄露还让苹果内部两条 AirPods 产品线变得更加清晰。

据彭博社报道，苹果内部至少开发过两个版本，代号分别为 B790 和 B798。

其中 B790 更接近现有 AirPods Pro 3，可以理解为在现有产品基础上加入视觉传感器和 AI 能力的版本。它原本一直存在于苹果 2026 年的产品路线图中，也是此次泄露视频中出现的型号。

另一个 B798，则是一代全新的 AirPods Pro，同样会集成摄像头，但硬件平台会进行更彻底的升级。

这解释了过去几个月围绕发布时间而出现的矛盾消息。

今年 6 月，消息称摄像头版 AirPods 已经推迟至 2027 年；但到了 7 月和 8 月，开发者又不断从 iOS 27 代码里发现 B790 的痕迹，一度让外界重新猜测苹果可能会在今年 9 月提前发布产品。MacRumors 此前甚至援引消息称，苹果内部曾讨论过将其命名为「AirPods Ultra」，而不是 AirPods Pro 4。

现在看来，这种可能性基本已经被排除。

彭博社最新消息显示，B790 原本确实计划今年推出，但苹果在夏季准备量产时遇到了供应链和软件问题。目前摄像头版 AirPods 已经从苹果 2026 年产品路线图中移除，苹果内部仍然预计在 2027 年推出。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/fb06a5ac-f95f-4b0c-9279-ab2b7b9a6a26.jpg)

### 但真正麻烦的，可能还不是技术

比发布时间更值得关注的，是摄像头出现在 AirPods 上之后引发的隐私争议。

泄露视频出现后，海外社交平台已经出现大量质疑，甚至有人直接把它称作「PervertPods」。

原因很简单：智能眼镜至少还能看到镜片和镜框，AirPods 却已经是一种高度日常化的设备。当一副看起来和普通耳机区别不大的 AirPods 具备视觉感知能力后，旁人很难判断自己是否正在被传感器捕捉。

苹果目前的解决方案，是从产品定义上限制摄像头能力。按照彭博社的说法，这些低分辨率传感器不会用于拍照和录像，主要任务是扫描周围环境，为 Siri 提供上下文。此前消息还称，苹果考虑加入指示灯，在视觉数据被传输和处理时提醒周围的人。(MacRumors)

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/79dc8f41-8d4f-4c9f-82dc-de74ce9559f2.jpeg)

但「不能录像」并不能完全消除隐私问题。

对于旁观者来说，真正需要确认的并不是设备最终有没有把视频保存进相册，而是摄像头什么时候启动、采集了什么信息、数据在哪里处理，以及自己能否明确知道设备正在「看」。

这也是所有 AI 可穿戴设备接下来都会面对的问题：当摄像头从一个需要主动举起来的设备，变成眼镜、耳机乃至挂在衣服上的传感器后，「拍摄」和「感知」之间原本清晰的边界正在消失。

苹果显然已经意识到了这一点。相比直接让 AirPods 变成一台随身相机，它选择了一条限制更多的路线，只让摄像头承担机器视觉输入。

但最终能否说服用户和旁观者，可能要等到产品真正发布后才能知道。

因为 AirPods 只是开始。

按照彭博社披露的路线图，苹果还计划在 2027 年推出首款智能眼镜，同时研究过一款可以佩戴在颈部或衣服上的摄像头 AI 设备。摄像头版 AirPods、智能眼镜和 AI 挂件，背后指向的是同一个目标：**让 Siri 获得持续感知现实世界的能力**。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E6%91%84%E5%83%8F%E5%A4%B4/ac9a4f5b-c977-41d3-bef7-698d117fce6a.jpg)

如果这些产品最终落地，2027 年可能会成为苹果近几年硬件变化最大的一年。

除了 AI AirPods 和智能眼镜，苹果还准备了折叠 iPhone、搭载触摸屏的 MacBook、新一代智能家居显示器、家庭安防摄像头，以及带机械臂的智能家居设备等新品。

所以这次意外泄露真正值得关注的，并不只是「AirPods 加了一颗摄像头」。

过去几年，苹果一直在尝试让 Siri 读懂屏幕、理解个人数据和调用 App；接下来，它准备给 Siri 再补上一种输入方式，让 AI 开始理解用户眼前正在发生的事情。

只是这一次，苹果需要解决的问题也随之发生了变化。

过去大家担心的是 Siri 到底够不够聪明。到了摄像头版 AirPods 真正上市的时候，苹果可能还需要回答另一个更现实的问题：

如果连一副耳机都开始「看」这个世界，谁来保护被窥者的隐私？

entries.title: iPhone X 彻底「停产」了，但我们还没走出它定义的时代｜明日后视镜
entries.content:
![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/%E8%8B%B9%E6%9E%9C%E5%AE%98%E7%BD%91%E4%B8%8A%E9%82%A3%E4%BB%BD%E9%BB%98%E9%BB%98%E6%9B%B4%E6%96%B0%E7%9A%84%E5%90%8D%E5%8D%95%E9%87%8C%EF%BC%8C%E4%B8%8A%E5%91%A8%E5%A4%9A%E4%BA%86%E4%B8%80%E4%B8%AA%E5%A4%A7%E5%AE%B6%E7%86%9F%E6%82%89%E7%9A%84%E5%90%8D%E5%AD%97%E3%80%82/2845b8f2-ff3f-47a6-8ba2-1c1fff9d0d02.png)

> 消费电子产品由硅驱动，却也遵循碳基世界里的自然法则：物竞天择，适者生存。
>
> 鼠标已年过花甲，形态上却几乎没有太大的变化。计算机 70 年历史，从一间房蜕变成家用电器甚至演化成每个人的囊中之物。
>
> 而像 BP 机、GPS 导航仪、iPod 更多的产品，还没来得及演化，就被其他产品吞噬而终成为一代人的记忆。
>
> 爱范儿《明日后视镜》栏目，我们将持续审视那些持续演化中的明日产品：它们从何种想法中孕育？又如何在变化中存续？它们如何塑造新生活方式，又如何被用户所改变？

苹果官网上那份默默更新的名单里，上周多了一个大家熟悉的名字。

iPhone X 正式被列入全球「停产产品（Obsolete）」名单。按照苹果的惯例，当一款设备停止向全球销售网络供货满 7 年，官方与授权服务商就会彻底停止硬件维修，也不再提供原厂配件供应。

虽然它早在 2018 年秋季就从苹果官网下架，[2024 年又被列入「过时 (Vintage)」名单](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/okc4v95MCf3baYC5hyXbew)，但由于全球运营商与授权渠道的长尾分销，苹果官方认定的「停产停供」节点一路顺延到了今天。对这台 2017 年登场的划时代产品而言，这标志着它在官方意义上迎来了彻底的「退休」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/4c6d36cf-e5b3-4cb3-978b-a02f30ccb545.png)

图｜苹果官网 ![🔗](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/11/72x72/1f517.png) support.apple.com/zh-cn/102772

一台 2017 年的手机，在 2026 年走完了生命周期的最后一站。巧的是，它的退场也正好落在一个很特别的时间点。

2017 年，初代 iPhone 发布整整十年，苹果选择在这个节点推出 iPhone X；如今，在 iPhone 即将迎来二十周年之际，这台十周年 iPhone 正式被苹果列入「停产产品」名单。

这样回头看，iPhone X 恰好站在 iPhone 前二十年历史的中点：前面是初代 iPhone 开启的第一个十年，后面则是它自己参与定义的第二个十年。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/68ef00af-9b20-499b-8400-c4fe809c5ecb.png)

图｜9to5Mac

回望苹果 2017 年秋季发布会，Tim Cook 站在台前说，iPhone X 将「奠定未来十年技术的路线」；

在宣传片的旁白里，首席设计官 Jony Ive 用他标志性的语气给了 iPhone X 一个颇具浪漫主义的定义：

> 十多年来，我们的目标一直是打造一台正面全是屏幕的 iPhone。一个能消融在体验里的物理实体（A physical object that disappears into the experience）。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/338d006e-602f-4f63-9a8c-d1326190a804.gif)

彼时彼刻，很多人觉得这不过是又一次常规的宣发用辞；此时此刻，在这款产品生命周期画上物理句号的节点再回头看，前者一字未差地兑现了，而后者，则变成了随后这整整十年里，整个行业一直在默默逼近、至今仍未完成的终极执念。

iPhone X 就是这样一道明确的分水岭：它亲手替智能手机的前十年收了尾，又替后面的十年早早画好了样板。

### 第一个十年的终局：正面按键的消亡史

初代 iPhone 最激进的地方之一，就是直接拿掉了手机正面的实体键盘。

在此之前，数字键、方向键、接听与挂断等实体按键塞满了手机的正面，BlackBerry 更是把整套 QWERTY 键盘做成了商务手机的标志。苹果却用一整块多点触控屏取代了这些按键，让键盘只有在需要输入时才出现在屏幕上。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/30534f13-c31e-498a-a1a1-c3c2548250e0.png)

图｜NYT Wirecutter

这个决定在今天看来理所当然，在 2007 年却远没有那么容易被接受。

iPhone 发布后不久，时任微软 CEO Steve Ballmer 就公开嘲笑这台手机。他认为 500 美元的售价贵得离谱，更重要的是，没有实体键盘的 iPhone 很难吸引商务用户，因为它「成不了一台很好的邮件机器（not a very good email machine）」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/46ac3bc1-9f8d-4532-9bbf-24d93951d843.png)

图｜Steve Ballmer 在 2012 年 Windows Phone 8 发布会现场｜Wired

站在当时看，这个判断其实有它的现实基础。邮件和短信仍然是手机最重要的生产力场景之一，而 BlackBerry 那套可以快速盲打的 QWERTY 键盘，恰恰是很多商务用户已经形成的习惯。

苹果相当于要求他们放弃摸得到的按键，转而相信一块没有任何触感的玻璃。好在，后来的市场很快证明，苹果这次激进的选择是成立的。

用户逐渐适应了屏幕键盘，实体 QWERTY 也开始退出主流智能手机。拿掉那块永久占据机身正面的键盘后，需要输入时，它可以随时从屏幕里出现；不需要时，整块屏幕又能完整地留给网页、照片和 App。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/a415c633-2254-4dde-a195-618a03a6194c.png)

图｜iPhone 2G

Android 手机厂商们后来走上了相似的道路，只是在很长一段时间里，屏幕下方依然保留着返回、主页和多任务的「三大金刚」按键。

三星甚至一路将那颗标志性的椭圆形实体 Home 键保留到了 2016 年的 Galaxy S7 时代。物理按键、电容触控与上方的屏幕，共同构成了那个年代一眼就能认出的智能手机正面。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/5d177ebb-0cf1-4290-bade-c584e972cf6b.png)

图｜Galaxy S II 到 Galaxy S6 Edge、S8｜Reddit @justsomeone330

十年间，键盘消失了，导航键越来越少，手机屏幕越做越大。

到了 2017 年，智能手机市场已经成熟得不能再成熟。当年全球智能手机出货量达到约 15.5 亿台的顶峰，各家旗舰尺寸逐渐收敛在 5.5 到 6 英寸上下，Galaxy S8 也赶在 iPhone X 半年前拿掉了正面的实体 Home 键。

各家都在把边框越做越窄，但鲜有人回答一个问题：当正面真的什么都不留之后，人们该怎么操作手机？

iPhone X 给出的答案，对今天的大多数人来说，熟悉到几乎不值一提。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/1dd84a36-9876-493f-8310-5c9a8bc84977.gif)

底部上滑回桌面、悬停进多任务、贴着边缘横滑切应用——原本依赖按键完成的几个核心动作，在 iPhone X 上变成了一套行云流水、符合直觉的手势交互。

而正是这套当年带着强硬意味写下的操作逻辑，在随后的几年里，不知不觉变成了整个手机行业共同沿用的「标准答案」。

面对这颗陪伴了用户十年的按键的消失，苹果在当年的官方广告里只是半带调侃地替用户问出了这个问题：

> 主屏幕按钮呢？

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/ba78941c-37b5-47e9-91ec-3dc822640c00.gif)

图｜iPhone X 官方宣传片

这句文案在 2017 年道出了无数人的第一反应。那颗圆形的 Home 键对用户来说太熟悉了：它陪伴了用户整整十年，按一下回桌面，按两下进后台，长按唤醒 Siri，有了 Touch ID 后，解锁与付款也都靠它。

它的逻辑简单到了极致：哪怕是第一次接触智能手机的长辈，无论点进了什么未知界面，只要按一下底部的圆圈，就能回到熟悉的主屏幕。

iPhone X 上市后，这种简单粗暴的确定感突然消失了。所有的操作习惯被一下子打散重组——

多任务需要掌握上滑时那一下短暂的停顿，控制中心从屏幕底部搬到了右上角，截图和关机的按键组合彻底变了。刚换上新机的人，常常还会下意识把大拇指按向那块已经空空如也的下巴区域。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/af015e50-9703-43e0-9d13-6bd64e8f15c9.png)

图｜iPhone 8 Plus 和 iPhone X｜Tom’s Guide

为了弥补物理按键缺失带来的不确定感，苹果在 iPhone X 上首次将触控采样率提升到了 120 Hz。

虽然屏幕刷新率依然是 60 Hz，但更高的采样率让系统能即时捕捉手指的动作。在底层非线性动画的配合下，界面的推开、悬停与横向切换，第一次有了贴合直觉的跟手感。

没过多久，Android 阵营也全面跟进了这套手势，屏幕底部的虚拟导航键陆续退场。如今再把一台 iPhone 8 递给新一代用户，上下宽大的边框和那颗圆形按键，反而成了需要特意解释的「老古董」设计。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/34b636fc-64a6-405c-8026-4f7755c699f6.png)

图｜2017 年末，MIUI 全面屏手势｜搜狐网

从 2007 年初代 iPhone 拿掉实体键盘，到 2017 年 iPhone X 拿掉 Home 键，手机正面的物理按键用了整整十年彻底归零。正面，终于只剩下了一整块屏幕。

### 被群嘲的刘海，背后是一整个时代

随着 iPhone X 一起发布的，除了定义下一个十年的交互外，最扎眼的莫过于屏幕顶部那块异形「刘海」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/81672a9c-b098-4f42-92ed-9f949525f425.png)

图｜Apple

在此前流传的各种概念图里，人们期待的未来是一块浑然天成的黑色玻璃，而真机亮相时，顶部却像被硬生生「咬掉」了一块~~，就像苹果的 logo 那样~~。

老对头三星也没放过苹果，制作了一系列名为「Growing Up」的对比广告，镜头里买 iPhone X 的排队用户留着一头滑稽的「刘海发型」。甚至不需要台词，当年围绕 iPhone X 最大的槽点已经写在脑门上了。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/ead188b0-834c-48b5-a6e6-74c9cd41f395.png)

图｜Samsung

这块突兀的刘海，实际上是一场无奈的妥协。苹果的苦衷，来自 Home 键消失以后那套全新的生物识别方案——面容 ID。

触控 ID 随着 Home 键一起消失以后，苹果没有像当时不少 Android 手机那样，把指纹识别移到背面，而是直接换成了面容 ID。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/5429ffe0-04c9-4d49-baa2-438a3b25cfa5.png)

图｜Apple

为此，屏幕顶部必须同时容纳前置摄像头、红外摄像头、点阵投影器、泛光感应元件等一整套组件。其中点阵投影器每次解锁都会向人脸投射超过 30000 个肉眼不可见的红外点，再由红外摄像头读取面部的深度信息。

有意思的是，几个月以后，奇怪的一幕出现了：市场上开始一下子冒出大量刘海屏手机。只不过很多产品学得并不像。

小米 8 就是当时很典型的一台机器，正面乍看已经很有 iPhone X 的「风味」，底部却还留着一截明显的「下巴」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/13fe97c5-49de-4fbe-8837-df0334c4b9e7.png)

图｜小米 8

秘密就藏在 iPhone X 的屏幕内部。

iPhone X 是苹果第一款搭载 OLED 的手机。OLED 并不是什么新鲜玩意，此前就已经在不少 Android 旗舰上铺开。

iPhone X 这块柔性 OLED 的特别之处在于，它还承担着另一项任务——收窄底部边框。

传统手机屏幕需要在底部给显示驱动等元件留出空间，iPhone X 则另辟蹊径，借助柔性 OLED 可以弯折的特性，把面板下沿向机身内部折回，将原本占据「下巴」部分的元器件收进机身内部，最终做出了当时罕见的四边近等宽设计。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/8f9f80e1-d5d3-4a89-970a-91518f9e3ad5.gif)

几年之后，OLED 从少数旗舰机上的昂贵配置一路下放，京东方等中国厂商也逐渐进入更高端的 OLED 供应链。今天再看，OLED 已经完全取代 LCD 成为手机屏幕的绝对主流，四边等窄也逐渐下放到中端产品线。

屏幕之外，2017 年这一代 iPhone 还有一处后来越来越常见的变化：玻璃背板回来了。

iPhone X 用上了双面玻璃和不锈钢中框，同期发布的 iPhone 8 和 iPhone 8 Plus 也从此前几代的金属背板换回玻璃，并第一次在 iPhone 上加入 Qi 无线充电。

此后几年，高端直板手机也越来越集中到相似的形态：正面尽可能被屏幕占满，背面是玻璃，中间保留金属中框，无线充电则逐渐成了旗舰机的常规配置。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/01ecf828-db42-4c38-bd41-3efe076cacd2.png)

图｜iPhone X 与胎死腹中的 AirPower｜Apple

这些东西单独拿出来，大都能在更早的产品上找到影子。iPhone X 做的，是把这些原本散落在不同产品、不同技术路线里的放到同一款产品上，再围绕全面屏重新组织成一套完整的体验。

苹果一直以来最擅长的——「软硬件结合」，在 iPhone X 身上体现得淋漓尽致。

当它卖向数以亿计的用户时，这些昂贵、激进甚至带有某种强硬意味的选择，却顺理成章地成了整个行业随后近十年的「样板间」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/592e2e03-5dcf-4854-af08-80ed8439e6a0.png)

### 下一个「iPhone X」，还会是一台手机吗？

如果把 iPhone X 视作智能手机前 20 年的中点，它开启的这第二个十年，呈现出了一种极为微妙的状态。

今天的手机比 2017 年强大得多：屏幕上了高刷，影像模组越来越大，芯片制程、电池与快充年年迭代，折叠屏甚至能把手机展开成平板。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/d6629f04-194e-4952-a29e-8ea62d0f31de.png)

但一个在 2017 年熟练使用 iPhone X 的人，今天拿起最新的旗舰手机，几乎完全不需要重新学习「手机该怎么用」。

我们依然在一块尽量铺满正面的玻璃上滑动、点击、在 App 之间穿梭。摄像头与传感器能藏则藏，暂时藏不掉的，就通过软件与其和平共处。过去这近十年里硬件参数翻了数倍，最底层的形态与交互逻辑却维持了罕见的恒定。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/6ef42205-1da1-4406-8c8b-8b1ac02f2f56.png)

图｜灵动岛｜Apple Developer

初代 iPhone 让人告别了物理键盘，iPhone X 让人告别了正面按键。每隔十年，都有一批原本被视为理所当然的物理结构从设备上彻底蒸发，成为历史名词。

即将到来的 2027 年，恰好又是 iPhone 诞生 20 周年，距离 iPhone X 发布也过去了整整十年。

目前关于 20 周年款 iPhone 的行业传闻，听起来与 2016 年人们想象 iPhone X 时如出一辙：更极致的边框、更纯粹的玻璃，把 Face ID 和前置镜头彻底埋入屏下，做出一台正面完全没有任何开孔的「真·全面屏手机」。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/59761951-9a08-499d-844a-4e94b9d7b4e6.png)

图｜iPhone 20 假想图｜Notebookcheck，经过修改

如果这些传闻成真，当年 Jony Ive 在 iPhone X 宣传片里描绘的那台正面全是屏幕、最终「消融在体验里」的设备，也算在十年后补上了最后一块拼图。

只是到了 2027 年，仅凭这块玻璃，或许已经不足以再次定义下一个十年了。

AI 正在尝试击碎「解锁手机、翻找 App、层层点击」这套沿用了十几年的图形交互逻辑，越来越多的意图开始通过语音与环境感知在后台静默完成。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/3c7aa0be-7f8f-4a1b-9aca-3165e5fd23c8.png)

图｜Humane AI Pin

与此同时，智能眼镜试图把画面直接投射到眼前，智能耳机待在耳边，各家公司都在尝试打造挂在胸前、甚至根本不再配备传统屏幕的新形态终端。

苹果自身也在向外寻找答案。从 Vision Pro 对空间计算的试探，到关于智能眼镜与穿戴设备的传闻，手机并不会一夜之间消失，但它第一次需要回答一个比「下一代手机怎么做」更深远的问题：

> 未来的人类，还会像过去二十年一样，每隔几分钟就从口袋里掏出一块「发光的玻璃」吗？

Jony Ive 离开苹果后的选择，让这种历史的转向更加耐人寻味。2017 年，他还在为 iPhone X 描摹那块消融于体验的终极玻璃；如今，他与 Sam Altman 及 OpenAI 站在一起，正在研发一种完全属于 AI 时代的全新硬件。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/a53965c5-486a-4951-b966-898d8ec599a0.png)

图｜OpenAI

OpenAI 在解释双方合作时曾直言，计算机已经具备了看见、思考和理解的能力，但人类与计算机交互的方式，依然被禁锢在传统的产品与屏幕形态之中。

这也给 2027 年那台所谓的「20 周年 iPhone」留下了一个更难回答的命题。苹果当然有能力靠成熟的工业体系隐藏最后的镜头、削去最后的边框，把十年前留下的遗憾彻底补齐；但如果想再次拥有 2017 年那种重塑整个行业的力量，仅仅完成十年前的设计夙愿显然已经不够了。

2007 年的人很难想象，一块没有实体键盘的玻璃会取代「邮件机器」；站在今天，我们或许也很难想象，下一代计算设备何以不再围绕手机和屏幕展开。

当年 iPhone X 作为「One More Thing…」压轴登场，给智能手机的第一个十年干脆利落地画上了句号。如今，它也已经完成了自己的历史使命，正式走进「停产产品」名单；我们每天划动手机的指尖，却依然生活在它定义的时代里。

![](https://s3.ifanr.com/images/ep/uploads/lark2pad_upload/a7754a6d-30fe-41b2-885e-ab0b600fc015.gif)

当这个时代也走到下一个路口，人们真正等待的，或许已经不只是一台更完美的 iPhone。

在智能手机之后，下一个真正配得上「One More Thing…」的东西，到底会是什么？
